clue.text: Did wrong penetrating a female's secret

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the scrambled letters sit inside the female

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: done wrong, the letters of did are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone did wrong by breaking into a woman's private secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Did wrong' as misbehaving, but 'wrong' is the anagram signal acting on 'Did' alone; 'penetrating' says that scramble goes inside the female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept out of sight is a secret, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Hold your horses, love: right's missing out in 14

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scores, the letter O
R is right, and the possessive 's gives an S, the two letters that go missing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wait, love, as a right is lost somewhere in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' says that R and S drop out: the letters of HOLD YOUR HORSES plus O, less R and S, are rearranged by 'out'. 14 is EDINBURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palace of Holyroodhouse, the monarch's official Scottish residence, stands in Edinburgh at the foot of its main street.

clue.text: Turn in, my dear: we've got your milk

indicators.note: turn means change about, so the letters of in my dear are reordered

explanation.surface: A milkman tells a sleepy customer to go to bed, as the milk is on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn in' reads as go to bed, but 'Turn' is the anagram signal and 'in' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy workers are the people who supply and deliver milk, so they could say this phrase.

clue.text: Solver's in line for 26

indicators.note: in places the solver's word inside the line

parts.note: EL is an elevated railway line in American usage
thy is the old word for your, the solver's

explanation.surface: A puzzler queues up for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is PETROL: ethyl was the name for leaded petrol with tetraethyl lead added.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl was a common name for leaded motor fuel, from its tetraethyl lead additive.

clue.text: Model in island the Queen's exposed

indicators.note: in places the model inside the island

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
the Model T was Ford's famous car
ER is the Queen, and 's adds an S

explanation.surface: An artist's model on an island is seen naked by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stark naked is being wholly exposed, slang adjective for nude.

clue.text: Took head from head and won election

definitions.meaning: to top is to cut the top off, and poll is an old word for the head, so this means beheaded
coming first in a vote count

explanation.definitionFit: Coming top of a vote is winning it; read literally, topping a head is beheading someone.

clue.text: Unusual reserve with unusually icy centre

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of icy centre are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A cold heart produces a strange kind of reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says 'Unusual' because this form is a rarer variant of the usual word for reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rare variant of reticence, meaning reserve in speech or manner.

clue.text: Beast in time for slips

indicators.note: in puts the beast inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a beast

explanation.surface: An animal arrives in time to make some mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors in printing or writing, the plural of slip in that sense.

clue.text: Be angry? ____ funny side

definitions.meaning: the blank completes the phrase meaning recognise the humour

explanation.definitionFit: To boil with rage is to be angry; split in two it also fills the gap before funny side.

clue.text: In principle it has been put in 14

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the words principle it has

explanation.surface: In principle, the item has been placed in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is EDINBURGH: its port was merged into the city in 1920.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith, once a separate burgh, was absorbed into Edinburgh, so it has been put in that city.

clue.text: A boy in a dish that holds stationery

indicators.note: in places the boy inside the dish

parts.note: a pie is a dish
Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is sitting in a bowl used for keeping writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A papeterie is a case or box for keeping writing paper and envelopes.

clue.text: Tax actor in publisher's stock in 14

indicators.note: in places the tax and actor inside the stock

parts.note: a print run is the copies a publisher holds, its print
cess is an old word for a tax or levy
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous actor-manager

explanation.surface: An actor is taxed on the books a publisher keeps, somewhere in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is EDINBURGH, whose main shopping street this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes Street is the principal thoroughfare of Edinburgh's New Town.

clue.text: In 14 a stretch limo relay is unusual

indicators.note: is unusual tells us the letters of limo relay are found in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A relay of stretch limousines in the Scottish capital is an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' seems to describe the limo but belongs to the definition. 14 is EDINBURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mile is the stretch of road running from the Castle to Holyroodhouse in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Succeed at fishing, not rowing?

parts.note: read literally it means landing a crustacean while angling; to an oarsman the phrase means fouling the water with a blade and being jolted

explanation.definitionFit: In rowing the idiom describes a stroke gone wrong, so it is no success there, only for someone fishing.

clue.text: Virgin provided with Exocet is bad for blood pressure

indicators.note: provided in the sense of prepared, so the letters of the two words are made up afresh

explanation.surface: An airline armed with a missile would be alarming for anyone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin looks like the airline and Exocet a missile, but both are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive stimulation raises the heart rate, so something that thrills too much is bad for the blood pressure.

clue.text: Dine out on hot food raised in smelly old place

indicators.note: out means in disorder, so the letters of dine are rearranged
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so food is turned round

parts.note: grub is slang for food
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Eating out on hot food dished up in a smelly old place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DINE into EDIN; 'raised' turns GRUB into BURG. Edinburgh's nickname is Auld Reekie, old smoky.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh's old nickname Auld Reekie means old smoky, from its chimney smoke, hence a smelly old place.

clue.text: Not quite genuine about the French gag

indicators.note: about means around, so the trimmed word goes round the French article
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sincere means genuine
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French joke that is not entirely sincere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of the synonym for genuine, giving SINCER. 'gag' looks like a joke, but here it is something that stops a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer, like a gag, is a device that stops noise or speech.

clue.text: Say "good!" — she's going to China

parts.note: eg, for example, is what you write to mean say
she'll is a contraction of she will, so she is going to

explanation.surface: A woman shouts approval as she leaves for the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' seems to be the country, but it means fine porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is a very thin, delicate porcelain.

clue.text: It's fatty pork with new stuffing as a safeguard for transplants

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
suety means full of suet, fatty

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so new goes inside pork

parts.note: a pig gives pork

explanation.surface: Fatty pork with a new stuffing is offered as a safety measure for an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching tissue between donor and recipient reduces the chance a transplanted organ is rejected.

clue.text: 14 feature maybe in Spain whether I'm in it or not

indicators.note: or not means without, so the I is dropped from the Spanish region

parts.note: Castile is a region in Spain
I'm gives the letter I

explanation.surface: Something in Spain has a place in Edinburgh whether or not I am there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whether I'm in it or not' says the answer works with or without I: CASTILE is the Spanish version, the other the 14 (EDINBURGH) one.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh Castle on its rock is the city's most famous feature.

clue.text: (Formerly) British-controlled oriental island (part of)

parts.note: to run is to control
E is east, the orient

explanation.surface: A country once under British rule in the East, on part of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the sultanate was a British protectorate occupying part of Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei, a sultanate on Borneo, was a British protectorate until 1984.

clue.text: See 12
Sloth is so ineffective

definitions.meaning: the sloth belongs to the order Edentata, named for lacking teeth
lacking force or bite, as a weak law is said to be

explanation.definitionFit: A law without power to enforce is said to have no teeth; the sloth's order Edentata means without teeth.

clue.text: See 1
Sphere with 12 and a half yard circumference at the bottom of the ring

annotationWithheld.why: Sphere with 12 and a half yard circumference at the bottom of the ring (5,4): TEN + ORB + ELL fits, but nothing in '12 and a half' gives TEN (12-across is CATCH) and an ell is a yard and a quarter; no source for the clue found
annotationWithheld.clue: Sphere with 12 and a half yard circumference at the bottom of the ring

clue.text: Relative awaiting redemption?

definitions.meaning: slang for the pawnbroker, where pledged goods wait to be redeemed

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls the pawnbroker by this family term, so goods there await redemption.

clue.text: Twelfth Night without an endless meal — it grows on trees

indicators.note: without means minus, so an is taken from the feast

parts.note: Epiphany falls on Twelfth Night, the end of Christmas
taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the last letter goes

parts.note: tea is a meal

explanation.surface: Twelfth Night passes without a full meal, and something grows on the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: EPIPHANY less AN gives EPIPHY; 'endless' cuts TEA to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphyte is a plant that grows on another plant, such as a tree, without feeding on it.

clue.text: Gas over water?

parts.note: gas is the American word for motor fuel, and the question hints at the stormy seabird, named after St Peter walking on water, whose name sounds the same

explanation.definitionFit: Gasoline in American usage is this motor fuel, and its near namesake flies over the sea.
